Antecedent-wetness fuel curing: mean-normalised flammability from EMA of preceding monthly precipitation, sharpening the seasonal cycle without changing annual burned total; fuel-depletion state tested and pruned

Percolation spread: threshold-like fuel-connectivity multiplier on fire rate, mean-normalised, to restore the observed spatial dynamic range (low-burn cells overpredicted 5-58x, hotspots underpredicted 0.2-0.6x)

Fix output-transform ceiling: (1-exp(-rate))/12 capped monthly burned fraction at 8.33% while observed peaks reach 18.7% (nhaf Dec), 11.6% (shaf Aug), 9.8% (seas Mar); apply Poisson exceedance to the month itself with searchable month_scale
One-month flammability lag: blend previous month's assembled fire rate forward, since observed African fire peaks one month after the rainfall minimum and no driver peaks in the observed peak month
Sharper percolation exponent (spread_k 2.70 to 5.2): starve marginal cells still overpredicted 43-57x in Africa and return burning to hotspots underpredicted 0.62-0.78x
Limiting-factor (soft-minimum) combination replacing the multiplicative favourability product: fire follows the scarcest requirement rather than the product of all four climate factors
Coordinate-swept lag weight (0.14 to 0.213) after the limiting-factor change altered how the assembled rate responds to a shifted month
Cropland fuel-continuity suppression from LUH2: quadratic damping on cropland fraction, the first human land-use term in the model

Neighbour flammability coupling: blend a quarter of the four-neighbour assembled rate into each cell, the first non-pointwise term in the model; weight chosen for regional spread over peak global score
Eight-neighbour flammability coupling: corners weighted equally with edges since fire fronts do not follow grid axes; wider kernel supports nb_w 0.25 to 0.35
Multi-year fuel accumulation: slow EMA stock over the model's own fire rate, applied through each cell's long-run mean so unburnt landscapes carry more load
Agricultural stubble burning: cropland-gated ignition on the growing-season temperature shoulder, targeting the April peak in Central Asia that no climate driver explains
Rangeland management burning: rangeland fraction gated on a hot-dry-season temperature window, distinct in timing from crop stubble clearing

Wind-on-dry-fuel spread interaction: monthly wind anomaly gated on dryness anomaly, since wind drives spread only where fuel is cured; pointwise wind is worthless (free_resid 0.003, 23rd of 24 inputs) but the interaction gains
Joint retune of neighbour coupling (nb_w 0.35 to 0.55), lag weight (0.213 to 0.16) and gust reference wind (3.0 to 3.5 m/s); the wider coupling kernel is what the new wind interaction wanted

Vapour pressure deficit as fine-fuel moisture: mean-normalised flammability from atmospheric moisture demand, the strongest remaining residual signal (weighted r=-0.248) and better phase-aligned with observed burning than dryness
